newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CCC SAYS NEEDS EXPORT SUPPORT,WARNS OF DEVAL.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CCC SAYS NEEDS EXPORT SUPPORT,WARNS OF DEVAL.

text.p: The expanding Czech trade deficit will force a devaluation of the crown if the government does not act to spur exports, the President of the Czech Chamber of Commerce (CCC) said on Tuesday.

Zdenek Somr told a news conference at the Brno Engineering Fair that the government must do more to support exports from small and medium sized Czech companies, or a devaluation could be needed "within months".

"The situation is not very rosy. We could say this will come in several years, (but) the change in the trade deficit trend must come in several months or there will be nothing to finance such a large gap," Somr said.

Somr said the government has made a stable crown the cornerstone of its economic restructuring, "but if there is no money to finance the deficit, not even from the capital account, there will have to be a devaluation".

He added that he expected the deficit exceed 150 billion crowns this year. The deficit for the first seven months of the year stood at 85.3 billion crowns, and some analyst forecasts say it could rise above 160 billion crowns by the end of 1996.

At the fair's opening ceremony, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said the government and the central bank were prepared to maintain the policies that have made the crown one of the former East Bloc's strongest, and most stable currencies.
Somr also criticised a lack of state support for exports of small and medium-sized companies, which are not able to finance promotion and marketing abroad alone.
He proposed the creation of a special agency which would help small businesses to export or provide subsidies for the services of trade firms.
"It is necessary to separate support for large and small exporters. The agency would be a good contribution for exports to neighbouring countries and the rest of Europe," he said.
